## Purpose
`bash_command_gate.rs` is the orchestration face that chains sibling gate functions (`safety::bash_safety`, `pr_body_gate::pr_body_stale_gate`, etc.) in a fixed, documented order — the first gate to reach a decisive verdict wins, others return `None` and the chain continues. Each sibling gate lives in its own file (one behavior each), is a plain function (not a struct implementing `Check`) returning `Option<Verdict>`, and the family's single `Check`/`Observer` impl lives only in the dispatcher module.

## Convention
Folder: apps/rt/src/hooks/bash/**, apps/rt/src/hooks/write/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 14
`bash_command_gate.rs`'s header enumerates every sibling gate and the exact evaluation order; `pr_body_gate.rs` shows the per-gate shape: a `pub(super) fn <name>_gate(command: &str, cwd: &str) -> Option<Verdict>` that is fail-open at every early-return (`?`/`let-else`) and speaks only on a positive observation — never blocking by default (returns `Warn`, not `Deny`, unless the gate doc explicitly justifies a hard block like `bash_safety`). Each gate file's header explains WHY the gate exists (the concrete failure it closes) before HOW.

## How to apply
A new Bash/Write gate is its own file under `hooks/bash/` or `hooks/write/` with one `pub(super) fn <name>_gate(...) -> Option<Verdict>`, registered into the dispatcher's fixed evaluation-order chain in `bash_command_gate.rs` (or the `hooks/write` equivalent) — never implementing `Check` itself. Document in the new file's header why the gate is advisory (`Warn`) vs blocking (`Deny`), matching `pr_body_gate.rs`'s explicit "Advisory, never blocking" section.
